title: Disable acceptance of all IPv4 redirected packets
description: Disable acceptance of all redirected packets these prevents Man-in-the-Middle attacks.

title: Install auditd
description: auditd provides extended logging capabilities on recent distributions

title: ICMP ratemask
description: Ratemask is a logical OR of all ICMP codes to rate limit

title: Disable acceptance of all secure redirected packets
description: Disable acceptance of all secure redirected packets these prevents Man-in-the-Middle attacks.

title: Do not install tftp server
description: tftp-server provides little security http://www.nsa.gov/ia/_files/os/redhat/rhel5-guide-i731.pdf, Chapter 3.2.5
command: not c:dpkg -s tftp-server -> r:install ok installed;

title: Unique uid and gid
description: Check for unique uids gids
command:
c:cut -d: -f3 /etc/passwd | sort | uniq -d -> r:^$;
c:cut -d: -f3 /etc/group | sort | uniq -d -> r:^$;

title: Check for SUID/ SGID blacklist
description: Find blacklisted SUID and SGID files to ensure that no rogue SUID and SGID files have been introduced into the system

title: Disable loading kernel modules
description: The sysctl key kernel.modules_disabled is very straightforward. If it contains a '1' it will disable loading new modules, where a '0' will still allow loading them. Using this option will be a great protection against loading malicious kernel modules.

title: Check login.defs - RedHat specific
description: Check owner and permissions for login.defs. Also check the configured PATH variable and umask in login.defs

title: Disable acceptance of all IPv6 redirected packets
description: Disable acceptance of all redirected packets these prevents Man-in-the-Middle attacks.

title: kernel.randomize_va_space
description: kernel.randomize_va_space

title: Disable log martians
description: log_martians can cause a denial of service attack to the host

title: Disable learning Hop limit from router advertisement
description: The accept_ra_defrtr setting controls whether the system will accept Hop Limit settings from a router advertisement. Setting it to 0 prevents a router from changing your default IPv6 Hop Limit for outgoing packets.

title: ICMP ratelimit
description: icmp_ratelimit defines how many packets that match the icmp_ratemask per second

title: ICMP echo ignore broadcasts
description: Blocking ICMP ECHO requests to broadcast addresses

title: Shared Media IP Architecture
description: Send(router) or accept(host) RFC1620 shared media redirects. If it is not set the kernel does not assume that different subnets on this device can communicate directly.

title: Protection against SYN flood attacks
description: A SYN-Attack is a denial of service (DoS) attack that consumes resources on your system forcing you to reboot.

title: Disable IPv6 if it is not needed
description: Disable IPv6 if it is not needed

title: CIS: Additional process hardening
description: 1.5.4 Ensure prelink is disabled
command: not c:dpkg -s prelink -> r:install ok installed;

title: IPv6 Forwarding
description: If you're not intending for your system to forward traffic between interfaces, or if you only have a single interface, the forwarding function must be disable.

title: Disable the system`s acceptance of router advertisement
description: Setting controls whether the system will accept router advertisement

title: Protect log-directory
description: The log-directory /var/log should belong to root

title: Check owner and permissions for /etc/passwd
description: Check periodically the owner and permissions for /etc/passwd

title: Assign one global unicast IPv6 addresses to each interface
description: The max_addresses setting determines how many global unicast IPv6 addresses can be assigned to each interface. The default is 16, but it should be set to exactly the number of statically configured global addresses required.

title: Disable learning Prefix Information from router advertisement
description: The accept_ra_pinfo setting controls whether the system will accept prefix info from the router.

title: Entropy
description: Check system has enough entropy - greater than 1000

title: Install syslog server package
description: Syslog server is required to receive system and applications logs
command: c:dpkg -s rsyslog -> r:install ok installed || c:dpkg -s syslog-ng -> r:install ok installed || c:rpm -q rsyslog -> r:^rsyslog-;

title: Do not run deprecated inetd or xinetd
description: http://www.nsa.gov/ia/_files/os/redhat/rhel5-guide-i731.pdf, Chapter 3.2.1
command:
not c:dpkg -s inetd -> r:install ok installed;
not c:dpkg -s xinetd -> r:install ok installed;

title: CIS: Disable unused filesystems
description: 1.1.1 Ensure mounting of cramfs, freevxfs, jffs2, hfs, hfsplus, squashfs, udf, FAT

title: Dot in PATH variable
description: Do not include the current working directory in PATH variable. This makes it easier for an attacker to gain extensive rigths by executing a Trojan program

title: ARP announce
description: Always use the best local address for this target. In this mode we ignore the source address in the IP packet and try to select local address that we prefer for talks with	the target host.

title: Secure Core Dumps - dump settings
description: Ensure that core dumps can never be made by setuid programs

title: Disable IPv6 autoconfiguration
description: The autoconf setting controls whether router advertisements can cause the system to assign a global unicast address to an interface.

title: Secure Core Dumps - dump path
description: Ensure that core dumps are done with fully qualified path

title: Disable neighbor solicitations to send out per address
description: The dad_transmits setting determines how many neighbor solicitations to send out per address (global and link-local) when bringing up an interface to ensure the desired address is unique on the network.

title: ICMP ignore bogus error responses
description: Sometimes routers send out invalid responses to broadcast frames. This is a violation of RFC 1122 and the kernel will logged this. To avoid filling up your logfile with unnecessary stuff, you can tell the kernel not to issue these warnings

title: Disable Accept Router Preference from router advertisement
description: Disable Accept Router Preference from router advertisement

title: Check owner and permissions for /etc/shadow
description: Check periodically the owner and permissions for /etc/shadow

title: Trusted hosts login
description: hosts.equiv file is a weak implemenation of authentication. Disabling the hosts.equiv support helps to prevent users from subverting the system's normal access control mechanisms of the system.

title: Do not install Telnet server
description: Telnet protocol uses unencrypted communication, that means the password and other sensitive data are unencrypted. http://www.nsa.gov/ia/_files/os/redhat/rhel5-guide-i731.pdf, Chapter 3.2.2
command: not c:dpkg -s telnetd -> r:install ok installed;

title: TCP timestamps
description: It is possible to estimate the current uptime of a Linux system. It's preferable to disable TCP timestamps on your systems.

title: Disable sending of redirects packets
description: Disable sending of redirects packets

title: ARP ignore
description: Reply only if the target IP address is local address configured on the incoming interface.

title: Magic SysRq
description: Kernel.sysreg is a 'magical' key combo you can hit which the kernel will respond to regardless of whatever else it is doing, unless it is completely locked up.

title: Reverse path filtering
description: The rp_filter can reject incoming packets if their source address doesn't match the network interface that they're arriving on, which helps to prevent IP spoofing.

title: TCP RFC1337 Protect Against TCP Time-Wait
description: This enables a fix for time-wait assassination hazards in tcp, described in RFC 1337. If enabled, this causes the kernel to drop RST packets for sockets in the time-wait state.

title: CPU No execution Flag or Kernel ExecShield
description: Kernel features and CPU flags provide a protection against buffer overflows. The CPU NX Flag and the kernel parameter exec-shield prevents code execution on a per memory page basis. If the CPU supports the NX-Flag then this should be used instead of the kernel parameter exec-shield.

title: Do not install rsh server
description: The r-commands suffers same problem as telnet. http://www.nsa.gov/ia/_files/os/redhat/rhel5-guide-i731.pdf, Chapter 3.2.3
command: not c:dpkg -s rsh-server -> r:install ok installed;

title: IPv4 Forwarding
description: If you're not intending for your system to forward traffic between interfaces, or if you only have a single interface, the forwarding function must be disable.

title: Disable Source Routing
description: The accept_source_route option causes network interfaces to accept packets with the Strict Source Route (SSR) or Loose Source Routing (LSR) option set. An attacker is able to send a source routed packet into the network, then he could intercept the replies and your server might not know that it is not communicating with a trusted server

title: Do not install ypserv server (NIS)
description: Network Information Service (NIS) has some security design weaknesses like inadequate protection of important authentication information. http://www.nsa.gov/ia/_files/os/redhat/rhel5-guide-i731.pdf, Chapter 3.2.4
command: not c:dpkg -s ypserv -> r:install ok installed;

title: Disable acceptance of IPv6 router solicitations messages
description: The router solicitations setting determines how many router solicitations are sent when bringing up the interface. If addresses are statically assigned, there is no need to send any solicitations.

title: Check login.defs
description: Check owner and permissions for login.defs. Also check the configured PATH variable and umask in login.defs

title: Check for .rhosts and .netrc file
description: Find .rhosts and .netrc files - CIS Benchmark 9.2.9-10
